name: shell-coverage
//: The repo-level shell coverage gate: merges the bashcov record every coverage:shell project's test target writes (tools/coverage/shcov.sh run) and enforces the shell line floor once, over every shell script in the tree (tools/shell/shell.sh files). It depends on exactly what can move that number: the projects whose tests write records, and the driver. It is its own project, apart from the Rust coverage gate, so a script edit re-runs the shell journeys without re-running the instrumented Rust suites.

coverage.//suppression: llmlint: ignore-block[expensive_tests_stay_behind_their_own_edge] coverage-driver's whole test suite is cheap, not an expensive tier: its Rust-driver half (coverage.test.mjs) builds two dependency-free scratch crates offline into a fresh CARGO_TARGET_DIR on every run, so it is always cold, and measured 2.25s that way; the shell gate must merge this project's record because those same tests are what execute coverage.sh

options.command: bash tools/coverage/shcov.sh report bench ci-workflows coverage-driver live real-oneharness release-targets repo-tooling screenshots shell-tools

coverage.//: The projects named are exactly the coverage:shell ones (a workspace journey holds the two equal), so a record is never missed or read stale: each was just written or restored by the test it dependsOn. Uncached, like the Rust gate: a replay could report on records that no longer exist.
